sale_success: The till hums a happy little tune.
stockout: The crowd thins; you ran dry.
A dozen hands grasp at nothing.
You mouth an apology to the queue.
Bare racks stare back at you.
spoilage: The glow fades to a sad gray mush.
Fruit weeps plasma onto the floor.
A sour smell haunts aisle two.
Expired. The bin drones feast tonight.
upgrade: Your stall just got a little smarter.
Tools of the trade, freshly sharpened.
game_over: The stall lights dim one last time.
Eighteen days under the neon sky: done.
You close the shutters on the market.
The starport forgets, but you won't.
Final tally under a fading moon.
Your ledger closes; the crowd moves on.
Last call echoes down the dock.

balance_notes: Start cash buys a shallow spread, never a full 24-unit hoard.
Noodles sell quickly but rot in two days, punishing overstock.
Fruit doubles money per unit yet spoils; stock it before events.
Jerky and charms never expire, so they park spare cash safely.
Event headlines hint at tag spikes; buy the matching tags early.
Negative events cut capacity or raise costs; keep a cash buffer.
Capacity upgrades pay off only if demand is forecast to rise.
Reputation from brand upgrades cushions inspection and rivals.
Late game shifts toward high-margin charms for the finale.
tutorial_tips: Buy stock, set prices, then open the market.
Events change what customers want and suppliers charge.
Oldest stock sells first; watch every expiry date.
Raise prices on scarce goods to earn more per unit.
Cut prices before expiry to clear old stock fast.
High reputation attracts more demand tomorrow.
Campaigns boost traffic but can hurt reputation.
Cold storage protects risky perishable stock.
Do not over-order: spoiled goods burn cash and rep.
Keep a cash reserve for rent and supply shocks.
Match product tags to each arriving customer group.
Day 18 is the finale; turn inventory into credits.
